items.back: Liberalisation (delicensing), Privatisation (disinvestment), Globalisation (world integration); 1991 New Economic Policy under PM Narasimha Rao & FM Manmohan Singh (BoP crisis).
From producer/controller to regulator/facilitator/enabler ('steering not rowing'); slogan 'Minimum Government, Maximum Governance'; Ease of Doing Business.
Independent statutory regulators govern liberalised markets at arm's length: SEBI 1992, TRAI 1997, IRDAI 1999, CCI (2002 Act).
Minority sale (retain control) vs strategic sale (transfer management); nodal body DIPAM; strong PSUs get Maharatna/Navratna/Miniratna autonomy.
India a founder member of WTO (1 Jan 1995, from GATT); FERA 1973 → FEMA 1999 (forex violations became civil).
items.examPoint: 1991 reforms — WTO founder member (1995), FERA 1973 -> FEMA 1999

items.back: Statutory fiscal-discipline framework setting deficit-reduction targets; complements liberalisation; N.K. Singh review committee.
Abolished licensing for most industries; cut public-sector-reserved industries 17→8 (later atomic energy & railways core); MRTP relaxed.
items.examPoint: New Industrial Policy 1991 — delicensing; reserved industries 17->8; PSU Ratna grades

items.back: Competitive federalism (states court FDI, Ease-of-Doing-Business rankings) + cooperative federalism (NITI Aayog 2015, GST Council Art 279A, Inter-State Council Art 263).
Not abolished but targeted — JAM trinity (Jan Dhan+Aadhaar+Mobile) powers DBT; rights-based welfare (MGNREGA 2005, RTE 2009) expanded alongside markets.
Gains: middle class, services/IT, poverty decline. Costs: inequality, jobless growth, informal sector. Globalisation conditions (not eliminates) policy space (WTO).

items.front: Which DPSP targets concentration of wealth?
items.back: Article 39(b) & (c) — resources must serve the common good and the economy must not concentrate wealth to the common detriment.

items.front: Gandhism and Marxism converge on what ideal?
items.back: Both envisage an eventual stateless society — Gandhi via self-regulating village communities, Marx via the withering away of the state.
items.examPoint: Gandhism & Marxism — convergence on a stateless society
